Let \(V=\mathbb F_p^N\), so \(R=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb F_p}(V)\). Fix once and for all a nonsquare \(\delta\in\mathbb F_p^\times\).

For any subfield \(E\cong \mathbb F_{p^2}\) in \(R\), the trace-zero elements of \(E\) form a one-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-space. Every nonzero trace-zero element \(X\in E\) satisfies \(X^2\in\mathbb F_p^\times\) and \(X^2\) is a nonsquare. Hence each \(E\) has exactly two trace-zero generators \(X\) with
\[
X^2=\delta I.
\]
Thus the desired tuples of fields are the same as ordered tuples
\[
(X_1,\dots,X_{2m+1})
\]
with
\[
X_i^2=\delta I,\qquad X_iX_j=-X_jX_i\quad(i\ne j),
\]
modulo the independent sign changes \(X_i\mapsto -X_i\). So we count such normalized tuples and divide by \(2^{2m+1}\).

These normalized tuples are exactly representations on \(V\) of the Clifford algebra
\[
C=\mathbb F_p\langle e_1,\dots,e_{2m+1}\rangle/
(e_i^2=\delta,\ e_ie_j=-e_je_i).
\]
Let
\[
\omega=e_1e_2\cdots e_{2m+1}.
\]
Then \(\omega\) is central and
\[
\omega^2=(-1)^{(2m+1)(2m)/2}\delta^{2m+1}
=(-1)^m\delta^{2m+1}.
\]
Modulo squares this is \((-1)^m\delta\).

The even Clifford algebra here is \(M_{2^m}(\mathbb F_p)\), so the odd algebra \(C\) is:

\[
C\cong
\begin{cases}
M_{2^m}(\mathbb F_{p^2}), & (-1)^m\delta\text{ nonsquare},\\
M_{2^m}(\mathbb F_p)\oplus M_{2^m}(\mathbb F_p), & (-1)^m\delta\text{ square}.
\end{cases}
\]

Since \(\delta\) is nonsquare, the split case occurs exactly when \(m\) is odd and \(p\equiv 3\pmod 4\).

If \(C\cong M_{2^m}(\mathbb F_{p^2})\), then \(V\) is the unique simple \(C\)-module, and the stabilizer of one normalized tuple in \(\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb F_p)\) is \(\mathbb F_{p^2}^\times\), of size \(p^2-1\). Thus the number of normalized tuples is
\[
\frac{G_N}{p^2-1}.
\]

If \(C\cong M_{2^m}(\mathbb F_p)\oplus M_{2^m}(\mathbb F_p)\), then \(V\) can be \(S_+\oplus S_-\), \(S_+^{\oplus 2}\), or \(S_-^{\oplus 2}\). The stabilizers have sizes
\[
(p-1)^2,\qquad |\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|,\qquad |\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|.
\]
Therefore the number of normalized tuples is
\[
G_N\left(\frac1{(p-1)^2}+\frac{2}{|\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}\right).
\]
Since
\[
|\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|=p(p-1)^2(p+1),
\]
this equals
\[
G_N\cdot \frac{p^2+p+2}{p(p+1)(p-1)^2}.
\]

Finally divide by \(2^{2m+1}\).

\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{G_N}{2^{2m+1}(p^2-1)}, & \text{if } m\text{ is even or }p\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\[1.2em]
\dfrac{G_N(p^2+p+2)}{2^{2m+1}p(p+1)(p-1)^2}, & \text{if } m\text{ is odd and }p\equiv 3\pmod 4.
\end{cases}
}
\]
